_about: Golden fixtures for the parts of the field guiding service contract that are
stated as prose rather than as a wire format. They exist so that a later
service can be compared against shapes this client already accepts, and so
that the parts we had to guess are visible instead of buried in a stub.
Read the _guessed keys on each object. They are the fields this client had
to invent because the contract does not name them. When the service exists,
these are the exact things to check first.

_about: Rule 21: no species_code and no count, and the record is still whole.
status needs_review is deliberately distinct from pending. Pending
means nobody looked. Needs review means somebody competent looked and
declined to decide.
Rule 9: a deletion arrives as a tombstone in the change feed, not as
an absence. The row keeps its values and gains is_tombstone.
A feed entry need not repeat unchanged fields. Only revision and the one
field that moved. A client that treats a page as a whole record will blank
everything this leaves out.
A push is a bounded batch of operations. Every operation carries its own
operation_id, because that is the retry identity and never the entity id.
The operation is an intent, not a whole-entity replacement.

_about: A batch is not all-or-nothing. One result per operation, always, whatever
happened to its neighbours. This batch shows three of the four outcomes at
once, which is the case a client is most likely to get wrong.
A retry after an ambiguous response. The operation id was processed
already, so this is not a conflict and must not be shown as one. Note the
client's own entity_id is absent from server_state: the service's id is
not the client's, and conflating them loses the record of which came
from where.
A declared prerequisite has not settled. The same bytes are sent again
later; they are not rebuilt, because rebuilding them makes the retry a
different operation.
Rule 6: a conflict is decided by revision, never by a timestamp. The
refusal returns the current server record so the client can show what it
holds and what the service holds, side by side. The service never merges
and never discards the client's edit silently.
Verification is never resolved by revision. A stale-revision verification
is refused unconditionally, so retrying sends the same bytes to be refused
again forever. This one needs a person.
Rule 15: a correction changing species_code or count requires a reason.
Without one the correction is refused whatever the revisions say.
Rule: cache reference data aggressively. The contract does not name an
